about: Conformance cases for language 6.13 (callback `with` and `returning`), 6.14.7 (tuple parts) and 6.15 (sequences). Run every case of every suite through the host's own evaluation and compare with `expect`. Value encoding: numbers, booleans and strings are themselves; null is none and {"some": v} is some; {"tuple": [..]}; a finite list is an array; an infinite list is {"counter": {"from": a, "step": b}} as an input and {"prefix": [first 8 items]} as a result; {"variant": n, "fields": [..]}; {"ent": [key, id]} is an entity whose key `==` and the order see and whose id only `moved from` sees; {"id": n} is a host reference's identity. A result of {"undefined": true} is an operator with no value (size and reverse of an infinite list); {"undecided": true} is an equality no finite prefix refutes; {"refused": ...} is a form refused at build.

definitions.index: xs[i]: the element at position i; none when i < 0 or i >= count(xs) (for an infinite xs, when i < 0). Never fails.
definitions.take: take(n, xs): the first n elements, or all if fewer; empty when n <= 0.
definitions.skip: skip(n, xs): xs without its first n elements; xs when n <= 0, empty when n >= count(xs). skip(n, xs)[k] == xs[k + n].
definitions.slice: xs[i..j] is take(j - i, skip(i, xs)); xs[i..] is skip(i, xs); xs[..j] is take(j, xs). Never fails. Args: [xs, i|null, j|null]. Not exercised for i < 0, where the equation and the sentence 'positions outside the list are not elements' differ.
definitions.concat: xs ++ ys: for a finite xs, xs then ys; for an infinite xs, xs. Associative, [] is the unit.
definitions.reverse: reverse(xs)[k] == xs[count(xs) - 1 - k]; no value for an infinite xs.
definitions.map: map(f, xs)[k] == f(xs[k]); f a named pure function.
definitions.filter: filter(p, []) == []; filter(p, [x] ++ r) == (if p(x) then [x] else []) ++ filter(p, r).
definitions.zip: zip(xs, ys)[k] == (xs[k], ys[k]) while both exist.
definitions.scalars: the Unicode scalar values of the text, in order.
definitions.count: the number of elements; no value for an infinite list.
definitions.eq: equal at every position; for infinite lists, of every finite prefix: refuted on a prefix, never confirmed.
definitions.part: e.k: the component k of a tuple; a component the tuple lacks is refused at build.
definitions.bind: a pattern (a, _, b) binds a name to each wanted part; a pattern of the wrong length is refused at build.
definitions.next: yields: next returns xs[0] and leaves xs[1..].
definitions.present: present(xs, i): i >= 0 and (xs infinite or i < count(xs)): position i holds an element, whatever it is.
definitions.select: select(bs, xs): the elements xs[k] where bs[k] is true, for the positions both lists have.
definitions.while_true: while_true(bs, xs): take(n, xs) with n the position of the first false in bs, or count(bs); xs when bs is infinite and has none.
definitions.flatten: flatten(xss): flatten([]) == [], flatten([xs] ++ r) == xs ++ flatten(r); no value for an infinite outer list. map(yields, ys) reads a list of collections as lists.
definitions.runs: callback c : called by P.m …: the calls made during each call of P.m (groups); `with` and `returning` bind lists, one item per call; the count per call is checked per group. final(e) is read from the case's `final` environment.
definitions.lets: let name = e / let (a, b) = e binds for the clauses after it, once; a name already bound, or a pattern of the wrong length, is refused at build.
definitions.next_back: yields: next_back returns the last element and leaves all but it; no value for an infinite list.
